title: Operators choose the x264 preset, faster by default
description: Serves "The picture is as good as the device and the connection allow.". The owner (2026-11-19): operators choose the preset, deciding how much picture they give up for the compute they pay for, and faster is the default unless they choose another. JS-135 put the preset in the spec and priced it; this task adds the setting, makes faster the default and shows a viewer gains picture without losing a quick start.
acceptanceCriteria: A config key transcodePreset accepts superfast, veryfast, faster, fast, medium and slow; left out it is faster; any other value stops the start of every role with an error naming the key and the accepted values

Each new playback takes the configured preset; changing it and restarting gives new playbacks the new preset while a stream already playing keeps its spec's, and two api replicas configured differently each produce streams that play, because every later request carries the preset (JS-135)

docs/running.md gives, for each preset, the measured CPU against veryfast, the time to the first segment (JS-135's measurement) and the picture gain (VMAF from spikes/picture-quality), and says what changing it does to stored segments (new specs, the old swept as any unused spec)

In Octave (or, until JS-190 and JS-150, the native browser check), on the same worker: a start and a seek at faster get their first segment no more than 1.8 times later than at veryfast (the spike measured 1.42 to 1.49; medium is about 2.1), each time recorded in the run, and playback does not stall

A picture test on every tier, with ffmpeg's own psnr and ssim filters (CI's ffmpeg 6.1 has no libvmaf): a real-film clip encoded through the worker at faster, against its source under a 4 Mbps cap, has a higher PSNR-Y (the spike measured +0.27 to +0.92 dB) and a higher SSIM than at veryfast
The default change is listed under Changed guarantees: more CPU per viewer (fewer viewers per worker), up to about a second on a start on a full worker, a better picture

A 4K HDR tone mapped re-encode, with and without a burned subtitle, holds real time at the default preset on any worker whose measured capacity admits it (JS-161), or the default does not apply to it; the pull request says, from JS-154's figures, which machines hold it at veryfast and no longer at faster (D-038, D-044)
